source_title: MEDKids Diaphragm starter card (demonstration data, unreviewed)
primary_objective: How the diaphragm helps us breathe
educational_content: The diaphragm is a dome-shaped muscle under the lungs. The diaphragm helps us breathe. When the diaphragm tightens and moves down, air flows into the lungs. When the diaphragm relaxes and moves up, air flows out of the lungs. The diaphragm works without us having to think about it. Hiccups happen when the diaphragm suddenly tightens.
learning_objectives: The diaphragm is a muscle under the lungs.
When the diaphragm moves down, air flows into the lungs.

forbidden_claims.claim: The lungs are muscles that pump air
